results.title: World Fisheries Day: Making Ghana’s expanded Inshore Exclusion Zone work for artisanal fishers
results.content: For more than 22 years, Kwesi Atta has fished out of Ezilinbo, a coastal community in the Jomoro Municipality of the Western Region. The sea has fed his family and sustained his community. But making a living has become harder. Industrial trawlers compete with canoe fishers for the same grounds, and the tension sometimes turns into open confrontation at sea. What stands out in Kwesi’s experience is not only the competition but what he did not know. Neither he nor many of his fellow fishers were aware of the Fisheries and Aquaculture Act, 2025 (Act 1146), or that it expands the Inshore Exclusion Zone (IEZ) from six to 12 nautical miles offshore, about 22.2 kilometres. A major reform meant to protect artisanal fishers has been passed, yet some of the people it is meant to protect have not heard of it.
